newsitem.title: POLAND: Petrobank to boost its forex activity - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Petrobank to boost its forex activity - CEO.

text.p: Poland's Petrobank SA, majority owned by South Korea's LG Group, wants to increase its activity on the foreign exchange market and play a key role in Polish-Asian trade, its president said on Wednesday.
Dong-Soo Choi told Reuters in an interview that the bank would open a new department especially to trade on the foreign exchange market.
"Petrobank is the only bank in Poland owned by a Korean institution, so it could play a key role in financing trade between Poland and Asian countries," Dong-Soo Choi said.
"That is why we need to focus on the forex business first. We plan to create a new department at our bank to deal in foreign exchange markets," he said.

Dong-Soo Choi said that on November 7 LG Group would take up the 11,128,250 shares of Petrobank it had agreed to buy last June at 12 zlotys per share. The shares would give LG Group 50 percent plus one share of the bank.
He said Petrobank would also expand its activities in investment banking. "We are most likely to start with debt instruments," he said.
Dong-Soo Choi also said Petrobank needed to boost the number of its branches, currently at 10.
The purchse of Petrobank's stock by LG Group will boost the bank's share capital by 55.64 million zlotys to 111.28 million zlotys.
Petrobank, based in the central city of Lodz, ranked 24th among Poland's banks in 1995 with net assets of 85.7 million zlotys.

Its main shareholders are state-owned companies from the fuels and energy sector: fuel distribution company Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN), Belchatow lignite mine and Poznan-based power company Energetyka Poznanska SA.
